# Negation of a ball, one-limb center

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_neg_1` · proved for finite operands · proved for infinite and NaN operands · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A ball $Z$, of center $c_z$ and radius $r_z$, that contains $-x$ for every $x \in X$, with $X$ the ball of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$.

$$Z \supseteq \{\, -x : x \in X \,\}.$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-X` | `Ball<T, 1>` | `Ball<T, 1>` |  |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $c_x$ is a number of `T`.
- $r_x \ge 0$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $\lvert (-x) - c_z\rvert \le r_z$ for all real $x$ with $\lvert x - c_x\rvert \le r_x$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_neg_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/Ball2.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/Ball2.v), against `ball_neg_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_neg_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition ball_neg_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall cx rx : R,
  fmt emin prec cx ->
  fmt emin prec rx ->
  0 <= rx ->
  let '(cz, rz) := ball_neg_1 cx rx in
  fmt emin prec cz /\
  fmt emin prec rz /\
  (forall x : R, Rabs (x - cx) <= rx -> Rabs ((- x) - cz) <= rz).
```

## Infinite and NaN operands

The statement above is about finite operands. The claims also say what the kernel returns when its operands may be infinite or NaN. That statement requires:

- $X$, of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).

and then:

- **B1.** The result $Z$, of center $c_z$ and radius $r_z$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball, the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- **B2.** $Z$ is empty exactly when $X$ is empty.
- **B3.** If $Z$ is a finite ball, then $X$ is a finite ball, and $\lvert (-x) - c_z\rvert \le r_z$ for all real $x$ with $\lvert x - c_x\rvert \le r_x$.
- **B4.** No condition under which $Z$ is a finite ball is claimed yet: the claims list none, which does not say that it always is.
- It follows that in every case $Z$ contains $-x$ for every $x \in X$: the whole line contains every real number, and an empty operand has no points.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

**Status of this statement:** proved. Rocq checks the theorem `ball_neg_1_ieee_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBallCores.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBallCores.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_neg_1_ieee_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proofs of `ball_neg_1_correct` and `ball_neg_1_ieee_correct` depend on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** midpoint-radius negation (Milestone 1 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_neg_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_neg_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The negation of a ball with a one-limb center: exact, the radius unchanged.

cz = neg(cx)
rz = copy(rx)
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 1**: the runs of commit `6f89054` and the supplementary run of commit `f7e0b6d`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone1/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone1/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone1.md#ball_neg_1)).
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | smallest slack of the radius, in gaps |
|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 60 runners on 3 machines | 117 600 000 | 0 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 60 runners on 3 machines | 117 600 000 | 0 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 1 961 460 | 0 | 0 (`fp:7:-11:0`) |
| toy formats, every operand, supplementary run: 1 domain of 1 format | 327 | 0 | 0 (`fp:1:-5:6`) |

**Milestone 2**: the runs of commit `5f597fb`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#ball_neg_1)).
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | smallest slack of the radius, in gaps |
|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 200 000 | 0 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 200 000 | 0 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 6 domains of 6 formats | 1 961 787 | 0 | 0 (`fp:6:-10:1`) |

**In all**, the runs above:

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled, Milestone 1 and Milestone 2 | 124 800 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled, Milestone 1 and Milestone 2 | 124 800 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand of 6 distinct domains, each counted once, Milestone 1 and Milestone 2 | 1 961 787 | 0 |

The slack is how far the returned radius is above the smallest radius that encloses the exact set, in units in the last place of the radius: below 1, a radius one unit smaller would not enclose it.

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements of the statement on infinite and NaN operands.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
